title: Dispatch: PR #459 review fixes — migration guard + canonical conditions validation (attempt 1)
description:
Fixes for the two PR #459 review findings (review of branch eshyra-geny). Parent spec: eshyra-geny. Defect context beads: eshyra-q93i (migration), eshyra-gacz (doff gate).

Branch/worktree: this bead's id, cut from eshyra-geny.

## Finding 1 (High) — migration 0022 must not rewrite partial schedules

`packages/core/data/migrations/0022_stable_recovery_adoption.sql` currently matches stable-at-zero rows where ANY of the three schedule fields is NULL and overwrites all three. The only legitimate legacy state is ALL THREE NULL (canonical stabilization writes all three atomically); a mixed row is corruption whose surviving evidence must not be destroyed — the runtime resolver (hpLifecycle.ts resolveStableRecoveries) now deliberately throws on partial schedules, and the migration currently "repairs" them before that check can ever see them.

Required changes (edit 0022 in place — it is new on this unmerged branch, not an applied/immutable migration; CI/main have never seen it):
1. Adopt (roll=4/anchor/deadline write) ONLY rows where all three fields are NULL.
2. Abort the whole migration when any stable-at-zero row has a MIXED NULL/non-NULL schedule. Use the same guard style as the existing clock guard in that file: e.g. create a temp guard table with a CHECK (violation_count = 0) and INSERT the count of mixed rows, so a violation makes the migration script fail and the runner rolls back.
3. Migration test (packages/core/test/migrationLegacyAdoption.test.ts pattern): seed a stable-at-zero row with roll=1, anchor=500, deadline=NULL → running migrations THROWS, the schema_migrations ledger does NOT contain version 22, and the row's surviving fields are unchanged (rollback proof). Keep/extend the existing tests for the all-NULL adoption path and the already-complete-schedule no-touch path.

## Finding 2 (Medium) — doff gate must use the canonical conditions validator

`packages/core/src/state/attunement.ts` (inside assertInventoryCurseCustodyReady) hand-rolls a weaker conditions_json shape check: it accepts entries whose id is any string (including empty) and ignores extension values. `[{"id":""}]` is malformed per the canonical schema but passes, and with no matching curse id the worn cursed item is released — contradicting the fail-closed contract.

Required changes:
1. Replace the local array/shape check with JSON.parse + `validateConditionsJson` from `./liveStateSchema.js` (no import cycle: liveStateSchema is a leaf; mutateState already imports it). Wrap parse errors AND LiveStateSchemaError into the existing fail-closed MagicItemCustodyError messages.
2. Test in packages/core/test/inventoryWear.test.ts: seed the worn Demon Armor scenario, then write `[{"id":""}]` directly into character.conditions_json via SQL, and prove doffItem still throws (fails closed) even though no condition id matches the curse state.

## Verification

`npm ci` first, then `npm run verify:worktree`. Do not weaken existing tests. Commit on this branch only.
notes: Completion report: added a transactional migration-0022 guard that aborts on mixed stable-at-zero recovery schedules and adopts only all-NULL schedules; added rollback/preservation coverage. Replaced the custody gate's hand-rolled conditions_json check with validateConditionsJson, preserving fail-closed handling for JSON/schema errors; added malformed-condition Demon Armor coverage. Verification: npm ci; npm run verify:worktree passed (261 test files passed, 4 skipped; 4658 tests passed, 19 skipped). Commit: 136fb5d. No discovered follow-up issues.
